design_evaluation.summary: A polished, cohesive dark/light UI with strong hero hierarchy, clear navigation, and well-structured cards and modals. Main weaknesses are low-contrast secondary text, small icon-only controls lacking labels, and floating widgets (Voice Agent/chat) that overlap content on mobile.
strengths: Clear visual hierarchy on the home page: large two-tone headline, supporting paragraph, stats strip, and distinct primary (Live Feed) vs secondary (AI Lab) CTAs
Highly consistent component styling across views: uniform card treatment for the four tool cards, consistent pill badges, button shapes, and accent colors in both dark and light themes
Theme toggle produces a fully realized light theme with equivalent contrast structure (light hero, dark code panel preserved for legibility)
Chat consent flow is well designed: disabled 'Agree & Start Chat' until the terms checkbox is checked, plus a clear AI-disclaimer message
Login modal is well structured with Login/Register tabs, labeled inputs, placeholder hints, and a visible close (×) control; mobile menu provides a clear close (×) and full nav list
Status communication is good: LIVE badge, PASS/Warning states in the AI test result card, and per-card action links (Explore/Scan/Verify/Check)
issues: Low-contrast secondary text: muted labels like 'ARTICLES TODAY', 'RSS SOURCES', and gray card descriptions are hard to read on dark backgrounds and fail WCAG contrast targets
The Voice Agent floating widget overlaps the 'Reliability & Fact Check' card text on desktop and covers card content ('Adver...') on the mobile view, obscuring content
Icon-only controls (settings gear, moon theme toggle, chat robot button) lack visible text labels or tooltips, reducing clarity for screen-reader and sighted users
The 'Break it' nav item's purpose is unclear; red skull styling suggests a destructive action with no explanation
Stats are inconsistent across screenshots (5 vs 3 vs 11 'ARTICLES TODAY' for the same view), which may confuse users about data freshness
No visible focus indicators or keyboard affordances are demonstrated in any screenshot, and the chat panel appears as a floating layer without an obvious close/dismiss control in the open state
